summary.headline: Wonderla Q1 FY27 income rose 41% YoY to INR252 crore and EBITDA 39% to INR122 crore, with Chennai Park adding INR45 crore revenue in its first year.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as one of its best quarters, with income of INR252 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR122 crore (+39%) and PAT of INR72.79 crore (29% margin). Existing parks grew revenue about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth. Chennai Park, in its first year, contributed INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors, and management said it is tracking like a mature park for a Q1-type quarter. Management kept the new-park pipeline vague, saying an announcement on at least one park is expected before FY-end.

financial_highlights.value: INR252 crore (income); INR243 crore (revenue from operations)
INR9.47 crore (mainly interest and investment gains)

segments.name: Existing parks (Bengaluru, Kochi, Hyderabad, Bhubaneswar)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 15% on 7% footfall growth and 8% ARPU growth; contributed INR15.93 crore (46%) of EBITDA growth. Footfall: Bengaluru 3.43 lakh (+6%), Kochi 2.5 lakh (+6%), Hyderabad 2.9 lakh (+11%), Bhubaneswar 1 lakh (+4%).

segments.name: Chennai Park (new, first year)
segments.commentary: Contributed about INR45 crore revenue and 2.42 lakh visitors; EBITDA contribution INR21.86 crore, 64% of EBITDA growth. Management said about 40-50% of land is developed (around 30 of 61.87 acres).

segments.name: Resorts (THE ISLE, Terrea, Wonderla resort)
segments.commentary: Added about INR3.19 crore EBITDA (9% of growth); best-ever quarter for both resorts along with Hyderabad park. Resort EBITDA is not disclosed; resort-related 'other' segment revenue was about INR63-64 crore per the segment data queried.

segments.name: Corporate overhead
segments.commentary: Overheads rose INR6.5 crore YoY, mainly investments to strengthen the organisation; about INR1.5 crore incremental digital transformation (new POS from July) and about INR5 crore higher marketing YoY.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance given; management said the year has started strongly and it hopes the trend continues, but footfall is unpredictable quarter to quarter.
Chennai margins expected to converge with other parks over time; management said Q1 margins are tracking similar to larger parks, but a full year is needed.
Chennai will not reach 1 million visitors in year one; management said a couple of years are needed.
Mature-park growth model unchanged: low-single-digit footfall growth with most growth from ARPU; non-ticket mix to rise toward 40-50% (currently about 30%).
Management expects to announce at least one new park before FY-end (by March 2027); advanced talks with 3-4 state governments.
July footfall described as good so far, but management cautioned that it is only one month.
capex_capacity: Chennai Park capex about INR570-600 crore for 40-plus rides; Bhubaneswar park capex about INR190 crore.
Payback guidance: large parks 6-8 years; small-format parks 4-5 years (ballpark).
Capex allocation: about 10% of top line for expansion and new attractions; about 6-7% of top line for maintenance capex.

Structural capacity: large park can handle about 1.2-1.3 million visitors per year; small park (Bhubaneswar) about 5-5.5 lakh; management said capacity was about 1.1 million two-three years ago and is rising as rides are added.
Land: parks are 70-80 acres for large format; excess land is retained for resorts, extensions and rides.
Chennai and Bangalore share about 50-70% of rides; 30-50% are unique to each park.
demand_pricing: Footfall growth at existing parks was 7% in Q1, but management would not commit to sustaining it; May (highest-footfall month) had no unseasonal rain, and management said weaker monsoon was not a major factor.
ARPU growth is driven by non-ticket spend (+20% YoY); management said the 8% ARPU CAGR over 4 years leaves a high base, so similar growth may not repeat.
Hyderabad growth attributed to marketing and brand investment; trailing-12-month footfall was about 895,000 vs 893,000 a year earlier per an analyst's calculation, which management did not dispute.
Management cited headwinds: state elections in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, Gulf conflict, and F&B inflation.
Q1 and Q3 are the largest quarters; Q2 is the weakest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 7% ex-Chennai footfall growth sustainable, and what margin path should Chennai follow?
qa_highlights.answer: Footfall is unpredictable, but the year has started strongly. Chennai margins should converge to other parks over time, and Q1 is tracking similarly to larger parks.

qa_highlights.question: Will Chennai reach 1 million visitors this year?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said it would take a couple of years to reach 1 million visitors.

qa_highlights.question: How many parks will be added over the next 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans about 1-2 large parks and 1-2 small ones, with an update expected before FY-end. Parks will be picked based on land and government offers, and no closures were named.

qa_highlights.question: Is ARPU growth at Bangalore and Hyderabad a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium cohorts and in-park experiences drove non-ticket spend, which is the main ARPU driver. Management said the base is now high, so similar growth may not repeat each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Monsoon effect on Q1 performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said monsoon had little effect because June is weak and May had no unseasonal rain. Management also cited the Kerala and Tamil Nadu elections and inflation in F&B as factors.

qa_highlights.question: Will the resort model be replicated and is timeshare planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans to take the resort model to other cities, including standalone resorts such as Goa, but will wait a full year before deciding. Timeshare was ruled out in favour of retail.

risks_watch: Footfall volatility: management declined to predict sustainability of the 7% growth.
Chennai ramp-up and margin convergence remain unproven beyond one quarter; Q2 is seasonally weaker.
Hyderabad trailing-12-month footfall flat YoY, which management attributes to a lagged marketing investment.
Overhead growth (+INR6.5 crore) and marketing spend, which may recur; management did not call them one-off.
Monsoon and regional rain or disruption risk, including Kerala heavy rain and drought.
Timing and terms of new park announcements, which were not named and remain uncertain.
key_quotes: So this quarter was good, and we are hoping that for the remainder of the quarters, it will be good as well.
A couple of years, for sure. I mean, we will not reach 1 million in 1 year.
We don't give EBITDA for our resort business.
So we are waiting for a year to complete, then we'll take a call.
Once we close something, we will keep you updated, and we'll take it from there.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and the Chennai ramp-up, but cautious on forward footfall, which management repeatedly called unpredictable. Evasive on new-park specifics, resort EBITDA and the 18-month pipeline, citing proprietary information and no closures yet.
